docs.title: Step Engine (DX11GameEngine)
docs.text:
Step Engine (DX11GameEngine) is a modular 3D game engine written from scratch in C++17 and DirectX 11. It compiles from a single codebase into two distinct targets:

  • DX11Editor — A full visual authoring environment powered by Dear ImGui (Docking) and ImGuizmo, featuring live scene editing, asset management, non-destructive playtesting, and one-click game packaging.
  • DX11Runtime — A lightweight standalone game executable compiled with the DIST_BUILD preprocessor macro that strips all editor UI, mounts a packed binary .pak Virtual File System (VFS), and boots directly into gameplay.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text: Subsystem Capabilities Forward PBR & CSM Renderer DirectX 11 hardware pipeline with Cook-Torrance microfacet BRDF (GGX, Smith Schlick-GGX, Fresnel-Schlick), tangent-space normal mapping, 3-cascade shadow maps (2048x2048 Texture2DArray with 3x3 PCF and texel snapping), up to 16 frustum-culled lights, skybox cubemaps, and off-screen editor framebuffers. Entity Component System (ECS) Cache-friendly sparse-set registry via EnTT, 14 built-in components, intrusive doubly-linked parent-child entity hierarchies (RelationshipComponent), cycle-checked reparenting, and deferred entity destruction. Multi-Threaded Physics Jolt Physics integration running on hardware_concurrency - 1 worker threads, supporting Box, Sphere, Capsule, concave static MeshShape, and dynamic ConvexHullShape colliders, raycasting with OBB fallback, and thread-safe contact callbacks. Sandboxed Lua Scripting Embedded Lua runtime bound via sol2, supporting multiple scripts per entity with isolated sol::environment sandboxes, lifecycle hooks (OnCreate, OnUpdate, OnDestroy), collision callbacks (OnCollisionEnter, OnCollisionExit), and error-protected execution. Spatial Audio miniaudio backend supporting 2D UI/music playback and 3D spatialized emitters synchronized each frame with the active camera listener and entity world transforms. 2D UI & Typography Orthographic screen-space overlay pass for 2D sprites (SpriteRendererComponent) and dynamic TrueType text (TextRendererComponent) baked at runtime into 2048x2048 RGBA glyph atlases via stb_truetype. UUID Assets, VFS & Export Persistent 64-bit Engine::UUID asset ledger (enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json), RapidJSON 4-pass scene serializer, PAK2 binary archive packer/VFS mounter, and automated ExportedGame/ packaging.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OS: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (x64) with DirectX 11 runtime
  • Compiler / IDE: Visual Studio 2022 with the Desktop development with C++ workload (MSVC v143, Windows 10/11 SDK, C++ CMake tools for Windows)
  • Build Tools: CMake 3.20+ and vcpkg (can be installed automatically via tools\SetupProject.bat)

docs.title: Option A: Visual Studio 2022 (Recommended)
docs.text:
1. Bootstrap CMake & vcpkg (if not already installed): Run the automated setup batch file from the repository root: 

    tools\SetupProject.bat
    This installs CMake to %LOCALAPPDATA%\w64cmake and clones/bootstraps vcpkg at %SystemDrive%\vcpkg (verifying %SystemDrive%\vcpkg\scripts\buildsystems\vcpkg.cmake).

  2. Open the Folder in Visual Studio: Launch Visual Studio 2022 and select File -> Open -> Folder..., choosing the DX11GameEngine root directory. Visual Studio detects CMakeLists.txt and CMakeSettings.json automatically.

  3. Configure CMake & Install Dependencies: Select x64-Debug or x64-Release in the configuration dropdown. Ensure cmakeToolchain in CMakeSettings.json points to ${env.SystemDrive}/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake. On first run, vcpkg downloads and builds all packages in vcpkg.json.

  4. Build Both Targets: Select Build -> Build All.

  5. Building runs custom targets CopyShaders, CopyAssets, and CopyEngineFiles, mirroring shaders/, assets/, and enginefiles/ into ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin/.

  6. Building DX11Runtime triggers a POST_BUILD step that populates bin/RuntimeTemplate/ with DX11Runtime.exe and all required .dll files, enabling the Editor's Export Game button.

  7. Run the Editor: Ensure DX11Editor.exe is selected as the startup target and press Ctrl + F5 (Debug -> Start Without Debugging).

docs.title: Option B: Command-Line CMake Build
docs.text:
You can configure and build both executables directly from a terminal (or run tools\BuildGame.bat):

cmake -S . -B out/build/x64-Release -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 `
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$env:SystemDrive/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake"

cmake --build out/build/x64-Release --config Release

Compiled binaries are placed in out/build/x64-Release/bin/Release/ (DX11Editor.exe and DX11Runtime.exe).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• Core Engine Loop & Lifecycle — Initialization, frame update order, Edit <-> Play state machine, and dual build targets.
  • ECS & Entity Management — EnTT registry design, intrusive entity hierarchies, transform propagation, and deferred destruction.
  • Rendering Pipeline & Shaders — Multi-pass DirectX 11 architecture, PBR BRDF, Cascaded Shadow Maps, skybox, and 2D UI.
  • Subsystems, Physics, Audio & VFS — Jolt Physics integration, Lua sandboxing, spatial audio, UUID asset tracking, and PAK2 VFS packaging.

docs.text:
• Adding & Managing Assets — Importing 3D models, PBR texture maps, audio clips, TrueType fonts, and skyboxes.
  • Creating, Editing & Exporting Scenes — Viewport navigation, gizmos, Hierarchy/Inspector workflows, JSON scene saving, and standalone game export.

docs.title: ECS Components & Enums
docs.text: All ECS components and associated enumerations are declared in include/Engine/Components.h inside namespace Engine.

docs.title: Engine::MeshType
docs.text:
enum class MeshType { Cube, Sphere, Capsule, Custom };
Selects a built-in primitive mesh or custom imported mesh when attaching a MeshRendererComponent (also exposed to Lua as MeshType).

docs.title: Engine::MaterialType
docs.text:
enum class MaterialType { LitColor, UnlitColor, Textured };
- LitColor (0) — Shaded with Cook-Torrance PBR (BasicPS.hlsl) using baseColor, roughness, metallic, and 1x1 default textures; casts shadows. - UnlitColor (1) — Flat solid color (UnlitPS.hlsl) using baseColor; skipped during the shadow pass. - Textured (2) — Shaded with Cook-Torrance PBR (BasicPS.hlsl) sampling albedoMapID (t0), normalMapID (t1), and ormMapID (t2), modulated by baseColor, roughness, and metallic; casts shadows.

docs.title: Engine::CameraControlMode
docs.text:
enum class CameraControlMode { EditorCam = 0, Scripted };
Determines whether EditorCameraInputSystem processes fly-camera keyboard/mouse input for an entity (EditorCam) or leaves camera motion to scripts (Scripted).

docs.title: Engine::LightType
docs.text:
enum class LightType : unsigned int
{
    Directional = 0,
    Point       = 1,
    Spot        = 2
};
Matches the HLSL LightData::type integer values in BasicPS.hlsl.

docs.title: Engine::RBShape & Engine::RBMotion
docs.text:
enum class RBShape  { Box, Sphere, Capsule, Mesh };
enum class RBMotion { Static, Dynamic };
Configure collider geometry and Jolt motion/layer behavior (Layers::NON_MOVING vs. Layers::MOVING) on RigidBodyComponent (also exposed to Lua as RBShape and RBMotion).

docs.text: Field Type Default Description id uint64_t 0 Stable 64-bit entity identifier persisted as "EntityID" in JSON scene files.

docs.text: Field Type Default Description name std::string "" Human-readable display name shown in the Hierarchy panel and searchable via Scene::FindEntityByName. isActive bool true Master entity activation toggle. When false, rendering, physics bodies, raycasts, and audio emitters are disabled.

Intrusive doubly-linked hierarchy node. Managed via Scene::ParentEntity and Scene::UnparentEntity.

docs.title: Core, Scene, Systems & Serialization API
docs.text: This page documents the foundational identifier, math utility, scene container, ECS system, and serialization interfaces declared in include/Engine/Core.h, UUID.h, MathUtils.h, Scene.h, Systems.h, and SceneSerializer.h.

docs.title: Precompiled Core Header (include/Engine/Core.h)
docs.text:
Core.h is configured as the precompiled header (target_precompile_headers) for both DX11Editor and DX11Runtime. It includes:

  • C++17 standard headers (<cstdio>, <stdexcept>, <string>, <vector>, <cstdint>)
  • SDL2 (<SDL.h>, <SDL_syswm.h>)
  • DirectX 11 (<d3d11.h>, <dxgi.h>, <d3dcompiler.h>, <wrl/client.h>, <DirectXMath.h>) and #pragma comment(lib, ...) directives for d3d11.lib, dxgi.lib, d3dcompiler.lib, and dxguid.lib
  • Jolt Physics integration ("Engine/PhysicsManager.h")

docs.title: Engine::UUID (include/Engine/UUID.h)
docs.text:
64-bit random identifier used to uniquely track assets across sessions, JSON scene files, and VFS archives. Specializes std::hash<Engine::UUID> for direct use as a key in std::unordered_map.

namespace Engine
{
    class UUID
    {
    public:
        UUID();                       // Generates a random 64-bit ID via std::mt19937_64
        UUID(uint64_t uuid);          // Constructs from an existing 64-bit integer (0 = invalid/none)
        UUID(const UUID&) = default;

        operator uint64_t() const;    // Implicit conversion to uint64_t
    };
}

docs.title: Engine::Math (include/Engine/MathUtils.h)
docs.text: Inline math helpers built on DirectXMath and DirectXCollision (left-handed coordinate system: +X right, +Y up, +Z forward, NDC depth [0, 1]).

docs.title: Engine::Math::Ray
docs.text:
struct Ray
{
    DirectX::XMFLOAT3 origin;
    DirectX::XMFLOAT3 direction;
};

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Signature Description DirectX::XMFLOAT3 QuaternionToEulerDegrees(const DirectX::XMFLOAT4& q) Normalizes q, builds a rotation matrix, and extracts (pitch, yaw, roll) in degrees with [-1, 1] asinf clamping and ±90° gimbal-lock handling. DirectX::XMFLOAT4 EulerDegreesToQuaternion(const DirectX::XMFLOAT3& euler) Converts (pitch, yaw, roll) degrees to radians and returns a normalized quaternion via XMQuaternionRotationRollPitchYaw. Ray ScreenToWorldRay(float mouseX, float mouseY, float screenW, float screenH, const DirectX::XMMATRIX& view, const DirectX::XMMATRIX& proj) Unprojects (mouseX, mouseY) at NDC z = 0.0f and z = 1.0f (XMVector3Unproject) to construct a normalized world-space picking ray. bool RayIntersectsOBB(const Ray& ray, const DirectX::XMFLOAT3& position, const DirectX::XMFLOAT3& scale, const DirectX::XMFLOAT4& rotation, float& outDistance) Tests intersection against a unit DirectX::BoundingOrientedBox centered at position with half-extents 0.5f * scale and orientation rotation. Writes hit distance to outDistance. std::vector<DirectX::XMVECTOR> GetFrustumCornersWorldSpace(const DirectX::XMMATRIX& viewProj) Transforms the 8 DirectX NDC corners (x, y in {-1, 1}, z in {0, 1}) by Inverse(viewProj) with perspective divide; used by CSM cascade fitting.

docs.title: Engine::Scene (include/Engine/Scene.h)
docs.text: Central container managing the EnTT entity registry, play-mode backup registry, embedded sol::state Lua VM, entity factories, intrusive hierarchy links, and deferred destruction queue.

docs.text: Field Type Default Description registry entt::registry — Primary live ECS registry. Exposed publicly by design for view<> queries and component access. m_backupRegistry entt::registry — Snapshot registry used to preserve pre-play state during Edit <-> Play transitions and Game.Restart(). m_activeRenderCamera entt::entity entt::null Entity handle of the camera currently driving rendering and 3D audio listener orientation. m_lua sol::state — Master Lua virtual machine state shared by sandboxed ScriptInstance environments. m_requestQuit bool false Set by Game.Quit(); instructs main() to exit at the end of the current frame. m_requestRestart bool false Set by Game.Restart(); instructs main() to restore m_backupRegistry and reinitialize scripts after rendering. m_assetManager Engine::AssetManager* nullptr Pointer to the engine's asset registry for runtime imports and VFS reads. m_currentScenePath std::string "" Filepath of the currently loaded/saved JSON scene (empty if unsaved). m_entitiesToDestroy std::vector<std::pair<entt::entity, float>> {} Deferred destruction queue storing (entity, timeRemainingSeconds).

docs.title: Hierarchy, Lifecycle & Play-State Methods
docs.text: Signature Description void ParentEntity(entt::entity child, entt::entity parent) Performs ancestor cycle detection, detaches child from any prior parent, converts its world transform into local space relative to parent, and appends it to parent's intrusive child list. void UnparentEntity(entt::entity child) Removes child from its parent's sibling list and decomposes its cached worldMatrix into local TRS so its world transform is preserved. void DestroyEntity(entt::entity entity, Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager) Recursively destroys child entities, unparents entity, removes its Jolt rigid body, invokes Lua OnDestroy() callbacks, and destroys the EnTT handle. void SubmitForDestruction(entt::entity entity, float delay = 0.0f) Enqueues (entity, delay) in m_entitiesToDestroy (ignoring duplicates) for safe end-of-step deletion. void ProcessDestructionQueue(Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager, float deltaTime) Decrements queued timers and calls DestroyEntity on entries whose remaining time reaches <= 0.0f. void CopyToBackup() Clones all entities (preserving exact entt::entity IDs) and components from registry into m_backupRegistry. void RestoreFromBackup(Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager) Destroys active Jolt bodies and audio handles, clears registry, and restores all entities/components from m_backupRegistry with invalidated runtime handles. void StartPlayMode() Calls CopyToBackup(), runs ScriptSystemInit(*this), and switches m_activeRenderCamera to the first active non-editor camera. void StopPlayMode(entt::entity editorCameraFallback, Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager) Shuts down Lua scripts, calls RestoreFromBackup(physicsManager), and restores m_activeRenderCamera = editorCameraFallback. void InitializeLuaBindings(Engine::InputManager* inputManager, Engine::PhysicsManager* physicsManager) Opens standard Lua libraries and registers all engine usertypes, enums, and global tables into m_lua. void Clear(Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager) Destroys all Jolt bodies and audio handles, clears registry and m_entitiesToDestroy, and resets m_activeRenderCamera and m_currentScenePath. void GenerateDefaultSetup(Engine::PhysicsManager& physicsManager) Clears the scene and spawns Editor Camera, Main Camera, Sun Light, and a static 20 x 0.1 x 20 Ground box at y = -5.

docs.title: Engine::SceneSerializer (include/Engine/SceneSerializer.h)

Static JSON scene saver and 4-pass loader powered by RapidJSON.

docs.title: ECS & Entity Management
docs.text: Step Engine uses EnTT (entt::registry) as the backbone of its scene graph (Engine::Scene). Entities are lightweight 32-bit handles (entt::entity), components are Plain-Old-Data (POD) structs stored in contiguous sparse sets (include/Engine/Components.h), and behavior lives in stateless functions inside include/Engine/Systems.h.

docs.title: Component Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Every entity created via Scene::CreateEntity automatically receives three foundational components:

  1. IDComponent — A persistent 64-bit id used to serialize entities and rebuild hierarchies across save/load cycles.
  2. NameComponent — A human-readable name string and the master entity activation flag isActive. Systems (RenderSystem, PhysicsSystem, AudioSystem, Scene::CastRay) skip entities whose NameComponent::isActive is false.
  3. TransformComponent — Local-space translation (position), quaternion orientation (rotation), scale, a cached worldMatrix, and an isDirty flag.

Optional capability components can be attached in C++, through the Editor Inspector, or at runtime from Lua:

docs.title: Intrusive Entity Hierarchy (RelationshipComponent)
docs.text:
Rather than storing heap-allocated std::vector<entt::entity> child arrays on every entity, Step Engine links parent-child trees intrusively in O(1) memory per node using four entt::entity handles:

  • parent — The parent entity (entt::null if root).
  • firstChild — Head of the parent's doubly-linked child list.
  • prevSibling / nextSibling — Adjacent children sharing the same parent.
flowchart LR
    subgraph ParentNode ["Parent Entity (Model Root)"]
        P["RelationshipComponent<br/>parent: null<br/>firstChild: Child_0"]
    end

    subgraph Children ["Doubly-Linked Sibling Chain"]
        C0["Child_0 (Sub-mesh 0)<br/>parent: Parent<br/>prevSibling: null<br/>nextSibling: Child_1"]
        C1["Child_1 (Sub-mesh 1)<br/>parent: Parent<br/>prevSibling: Child_0<br/>nextSibling: Child_2"]
        C2["Child_2 (Sub-mesh 2)<br/>parent: Parent<br/>prevSibling: Child_1<br/>nextSibling: null"]
    end

    P -- "firstChild" --> C0
    C0 -- "nextSibling" --> C1
    C1 -- "prevSibling" --> C0
    C1 -- "nextSibling" --> C2
    C2 -- "prevSibling" --> C1

docs.title: World-Preserving Reparenting & Unparenting
docs.text:
Scene::ParentEntity(child, parent) and Scene::UnparentEntity(child) keep an entity visually stationary in world space when its hierarchy parent changes:

  1. Cycle Detection: ParentEntity walks upward from parent through RelationshipComponent::parent pointers. If child is encountered as an ancestor of parent (or child == parent), the operation aborts immediately to prevent infinite loops in TransformSystem.
  2. Detachment (UnparentEntity): Repairs the old parent's firstChild pointer and splices prevSibling / nextSibling around child. Decomposes child's cached worldMatrix directly into local scale, rotation, and position, and clears its RelationshipComponent links to entt::null.
  3. Local Space Conversion (ParentEntity): Computes the new local matrix relative to parent: 
    M_local = M_childWorld * Inverse(M_parentWorld)
    DirectX::XMMatrixDecompose extracts the updated local scale, rotation, and position into child's TransformComponent and sets isDirty = true.
  4. Sibling Appending: Emplaces RelationshipComponent on both entities if absent and appends child to the tail of parent's child list.

docs.title: Hierarchical Transform Propagation (TransformSystem)
docs.text:
TransformSystem(Scene&) runs every frame after physics, scripts, and camera input, ensuring TransformComponent::worldMatrix is up-to-date before rendering.

flowchart TD
    A["Iterate TransformComponent View (registry.view)"] --> B{"Is Root Entity?<br/>(No RelationshipComponent OR parent == null)"}
    B -- "No" --> A
    B -- "Yes" --> C["Recurse(entity, IdentityMatrix, parentChanged = false)"]
    C --> D["Build Local = Scale * RotationQuat * Translation"]
    D --> E{"Has Parent?"}
    E -- "No" --> F["World = Local"]
    E -- "Yes" --> G["World = Local * ParentWorld"]
    F --> H["Store tc.worldMatrix & clear tc.isDirty = false"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["dirty = wasDirty || parentChanged"]
    I --> J["For each child via firstChild -> nextSibling:<br/>Recurse(child, World, dirty)"]
  • Row-Major Convention: Step Engine uses DirectXMath row-major conventions throughout (Local = S * R * T and World = Local * ParentWorld), matching row_major float4x4 matrices and mul(rowVector, Matrix) in HLSL shaders.

docs.title: Factory Helpers on Scene
docs.text:
• Primitives & Empty Entities: CreateEntity, CreateCube, CreateSphere, CreateCapsule, CreateSampleEntity.
  • Cameras & Lights: CreateEditorCamera, CreateGameCamera, CreateDirectionalLight, CreatePointLight, CreateSpotLight.
  • Multi-Mesh Model Instantiation (Scene::InstantiateModel): Parses a .obj, .fbx, .gltf, or .glb file via MeshManager::LoadModel, creates a root entity named after the file stem (e.g., ABeautifulGame), and parents one child entity (<stem>_mesh_<i>) per sub-mesh with a pre-configured MeshRendererComponent.

docs.title: Cascading Immediate Destruction (Scene::DestroyEntity)
docs.text:
Calling Scene::DestroyEntity(entity, physicsManager) safely cleans up an entire subtree:

  1. Recursive Children First: Iterates firstChild -> nextSibling (caching nextSibling before recursion) and destroys every descendant depth-first.
  2. Hierarchy Unlink: Calls UnparentEntity(entity) to repair the parent's sibling list.
  3. Physics Cleanup: Removes and destroys any associated Jolt BodyID via PhysicsManager::RemoveRigidBody.
  4. Lua OnDestroy Hook: Invokes OnDestroy() via sol::protected_function on all initialized scripts attached to the entity.
  5. Registry Erasure: Calls registry.destroy(entity).

docs.title: Deferred Destruction Queue (SubmitForDestruction)
docs.text:
Lua scripts cannot safely call DestroyEntity mid-iteration without risking iterator invalidation. Instead, Entity:Destroy(delay) calls Scene::SubmitForDestruction(entity, delay), appending {entity, delay} (deduplicated) to Scene::m_entitiesToDestroy.

During Play Mode, Scene::ProcessDestructionQueue(physicsManager, deltaTime) runs after ScriptSystemUpdate and AudioSystem, decrementing timers in reverse index order and calling DestroyEntity once timeRemaining <= 0.0f.

docs.title: 4-Pass Scene Serialization (SceneSerializer)
docs.text:
SceneSerializer (src/Engine/SceneSerializer.cpp) persists scenes to JSON via RapidJSON while translating transient entt::entity handles into stable 64-bit IDComponent values and asset UUID handles.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as EditorUI / main()
    participant Ser as SceneSerializer
    participant AM as AssetManager
    participant Scn as Scene & Registry

    Caller->>Ser: Deserialize(filepath, scene, physics, assetManager, outError)
    Ser->>AM: Read JSON (from VFS if active, else disk)
    Note over Ser,AM: Pass 1: Asset Validation
    Ser->>AM: Verify every Mesh, Albedo/Normal/ORM, Physics Mesh,<br/>Audio, Sprite, Font UUID & Script path exists
    alt Any Asset Missing
        Ser-->>Caller: Return false + outErrorMsg (Active scene untouched!)
    else All Assets Valid
        Note over Ser,Scn: Pass 2: Clear Current World
        Ser->>Scn: scene.Clear(physicsManager) & SetCurrentScenePath(filepath)
        Note over Ser,Scn: Pass 3: Rebuild Entities & Components
        Ser->>Scn: Create entities, emplace components, populate idMap[savedID -> entt::entity]
        Note over Ser,Scn: Pass 4: Restore Hierarchy
        Ser->>Scn: Translate Parent/FirstChild/PrevSibling/NextSibling IDs via idMap
        Ser-->>Caller: Return true
    end

docs.title: Core Engine Loop & Lifecycle
docs.text: The application entry point and frame orchestration live in src/main.cpp. Both DX11Editor and DX11Runtime compile from the same main() function, using the DIST_BUILD macro to specialize startup, input routing, simulation state, and render targets.

docs.text:

docs.title: Core Asset Bootstrapping (LoadCoreAssets)
docs.text:
Regardless of build target, LoadCoreAssets() initializes shared engine resources and caches their UUIDs on g_scene via Scene::SetDefaultAssets:

  1. Fallback 1x1 Textures: TextureManager::CreateDefaultTexture generates primitive://white (255, 255, 255, 255), primitive://default_normal (128, 128, 255, 255), and primitive://default_orm (255, 128, 0, 255).
  2. Core Shaders: ShaderManager loads shader://basic, shader://unlit, shader://skybox, shader://shadow, and shader://sprite.
  3. Procedural Primitives: MeshManager builds vertex/index buffers for primitive://cube, primitive://sphere_..., primitive://capsule_..., and primitive://quad.
  4. Default Skybox: TextureManager::LoadCubemap loads the 6 faces under assets/Textures/Skybox/ (right, left, top, bottom, front, back) and binds the resulting SRV via Renderer::SetSkybox.

UUID Stability Note: In DX11Editor, AssetManager::LoadRegistry("enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json") runs before LoadCoreAssets() so virtual paths such as primitive://cube reuse the exact same 64-bit UUIDs saved inside existing JSON scene files.

docs.text:
Frame delta time (dt) is computed in seconds using SDL2's hardware performance counter (SDL_GetPerformanceCounter / SDL_GetPerformanceFrequency). Each iteration of while (g_running) executes four phases: Event Polling, Simulation Update, Multi-Pass Rendering, and Application Control.

docs.title: Smart Input Routing in Editor Mode
docs.text:
When DX11Editor is running, Dear ImGui intercepts SDL_Event messages first via ImGuiManager::ProcessEvent. To prevent camera controls from getting stuck or blocked while interacting with the 3D viewport:

  1. InputManager::ProcessEvent still receives events whenever !imguiCaptured, g_input.IsMouseCaptured() (right-click fly mode), g_editorUI.IsSceneFocused(), or e.type == SDL_KEYUP (preventing stuck keys if focus shifts while a key is held).
  2. During Render(), if g_input.IsMouseCaptured() is true, ImGuiConfigFlags_NoMouse is set on ImGuiIO so cursor motion while flying the camera cannot accidentally hover or click ImGui widgets.

docs.title: Editor State Machine (Edit <-> Play)
docs.text:
EditorUI maintains an EditorState enum (Edit or Play) toggled from the top Toolbar. Entering Play Mode performs an in-memory snapshot so runtime physics forces, spawned entities, and script mutations never corrupt the authored scene.

flowchart TD
    Boot(["Editor Launch"]) --> Edit

    StartPlay["Scene::StartPlayMode()<br/>1. CopyToBackup()<br/>2. ScriptSystemInit() (OnCreate)<br/>3. Select active Game Camera"]

    StopPlay["Scene::StopPlayMode()<br/>1. ScriptSystemShutdown() (OnDestroy)<br/>2. RestoreFromBackup() (reset Jolt & Audio)<br/>3. Revert to cached m_editorCamera"]

    Play["EditorState::Play (Simulation Mode)<br/>- Side/bottom panels hidden (Scene view acts as Game view)<br/>- Active camera switched to first active Game Camera<br/>- Jolt steps simulation & flushes Lua collision events<br/>- ScriptSystemUpdate & AudioSystem active"]

    Restart["Scene Restart<br/>1. ScriptSystemShutdown()<br/>2. RestoreFromBackup() -> TransformSystem()<br/>3. ScriptSystemInit()"]

    StartPlay --> Play

    Play -- "Click Stop" --> StopPlay
    StopPlay --> Edit

docs.title: How CopyToBackup and RestoreFromBackup Work
docs.text:
• Scene::CopyToBackup(): Clears m_backupRegistry and iterates every entity in Scene::registry, calling m_backupRegistry.create(entity) to preserve the exact entt::entity identifier (including RelationshipComponent links) before copying all 14 core component types.
  • Scene::RestoreFromBackup(physicsManager):
    1. Removes and destroys all active Jolt BodyID instances from PhysicsManager.
    2. Calls AudioManager::DestroyAudio on all active AudioComponent::soundHandle instances.
    3. Clears Scene::registry and recreates every backed-up entity and component.
    4. Resets transient runtime handles (RigidBodyComponent::bodyID = JPH::BodyID(), bodyCreated = false, AudioComponent::soundHandle = nullptr, isPlaying = false) so PhysicsSystem and AudioSystem cleanly rebuild fresh runtime instances on the next frame.

docs.title: Ordered Shutdown Sequence
docs.text:
When the main loop exits (ESC, window close, or Game.Quit()):

  1. Save Asset Registry (Editor only): g_assetManager.SaveRegistry("enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json") persists all known asset UUIDs.
  2. Clear Scene: g_scene.Clear(g_physicsManager) removes every Jolt body, destroys every miniaudio sound instance, and clears the EnTT registry.
  3. Subsystem Teardown: Shuts down managers in reverse dependency order: AudioManager::Shutdown() -> PhysicsManager::Shutdown() -> FontManager::Shutdown() -> ImGuiManager::Shutdown() (Editor only) -> Renderer::Shutdown() -> SDL_DestroyWindow & SDL_Quit().

docs.title: Rendering Pipeline & Shaders
docs.text: Step Engine implements a multi-pass DirectX 11 forward renderer encapsulated by Engine::Renderer (src/Engine/Renderer.cpp) and driven each frame by Engine::RenderSystem (src/Engine/Systems.cpp) and HLSL Shader Model 5.0 programs (shaders/*.hlsl).

docs.title: Render Targets: Editor Framebuffer vs. Standalone Back Buffer
docs.text:
Renderer::InitD3D11 creates a hardware ID3D11Device, immediate ID3D11DeviceContext, and a double-buffered DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM swap chain with a DXGI_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT depth-stencil buffer.

  • Editor Builds (DX11Editor): Renderer::CreateFramebuffer allocates an independent off-screen R8G8B8A8_UNORM color texture (D3D11_BIND_RENDER_TARGET | D3D11_BIND_SHADER_RESOURCE) paired with a D24_UNORM_S8_UINT depth buffer. All 3D geometry, debug wireframes, skyboxes, and 2D HUD elements render into this off-screen target (BindFramebuffer()), which EditorUI::DrawSceneView displays inside a dockable Dear ImGui window via ImGui::Image(renderer.GetFramebufferSRV(), viewportSize). Resizing the ImGui Scene panel dynamically resizes both ViewportComponent and the off-screen framebuffer.
  • Standalone Builds (DX11Runtime, DIST_BUILD): All passes render directly to the swap chain back buffer (BindBackBuffer()), and window resize events update both the swap chain buffers and the active camera's ViewportComponent.

docs.title: Physically Based Shading (BasicVS.hlsl & BasicPS.hlsl)
docs.text:
Lit surfaces (MaterialType::LitColor and MaterialType::Textured) use a metallic-roughness Cook-Torrance microfacet BRDF:

Lo(p, V) = (0.03 * albedo * ao)
         + sum_i [ (kD * albedo / PI + (D * G * F) / (4 * NdotV * NdotL)) * radiance_i * NdotL ]
  • Normal Mapping (TBN): BasicPS.hlsl re-orthogonalizes the interpolated tangent T against the normal N using Gram-Schmidt (T = normalize(T - dot(T, N) * N)), computes B = cross(N, T), and transforms the unpacked tangent-space normal (sampled * 2 - 1) into world space.
  • Fallback Safety: In LitColor mode (or when a texture slot is unassigned in Textured mode), RenderSystem binds 1x1 fallback textures (White albedo, flat (128, 128, 255) normal, and (255, 128, 0) ORM) to t0–t2 so shader equations remain branch-free without texture state leakage.
  • Multi-Light Culling & Sorting:
    • Supports Directional (0), Point (1), and Spot (2) lights.
    • RenderSystem::DrawEntities builds a world-space DirectX::BoundingFrustum from the active camera and culls off-screen Point and Spot lights using BoundingSphere(position, range).
    • Remaining lights are sorted by squared distance to the camera (with Directional lights given distSq = -1.0f so they always occupy the front slots) and capped at MAX_LIGHTS (16). If a scene has zero active lights, a fallback white directional light (intensity = 1.0f) is uploaded automatically.

docs.title: Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM)
docs.text:
Directional lights cast shadows across large scenes using 3 frustum cascades (Renderer::NUM_CASCADES = 3):

  1. Frustum Partitioning: Renderer::CalculateCascadeMatrices splits the active camera's [nearClip, farClip] range at 5%, 20%, and 100%.
  2. Bounding-Sphere Orthographic Fit: For each sub-frustum, Engine::Math::GetFrustumCornersWorldSpace unprojects its 8 NDC corners into world space. The engine encloses those 8 corners in a rotationally invariant bounding sphere of radius r and builds a light-space orthographic volume ([-r, r] in X/Y, with zPadding = 500.0f along the light vector to capture shadow casters behind the camera).
  3. Texel Snapping: To eliminate shadow-edge shimmering ("swimming") during camera movement, the world origin is projected into light space and rounded to exact 2.0f / 2048.0f shadow texel increments.
  4. Acne & Filtering: Hardware rasterizer SlopeScaledDepthBias = 1.5f plus a 0.0001f shader bias prevent self-shadowing acne, while BasicPS.hlsl selects the cascade slice using camera-space viewZ and performs 3x3 Percentage-Closer Filtering (PCF) (SampleLevel) for soft shadow penumbras.

docs.title: Skybox, Debug Colliders & 2D UI Passes
docs.text:
• Debug Collider Pass (RenderSystem::DrawDebugColliders): Active only in DX11Editor during Edit mode when the selected entity has an active RigidBodyComponent with showWireframe == true. Switches to m_wireframeRasterizerState (D3D11_FILL_WIREFRAME, D3D11_CULL_NONE) and renders the collider's exact physical dimensions in solid green (UnlitVS / UnlitPS).
  • Skybox Pass (Renderer::DrawSkybox): Strips translation from the camera view matrix, scales the unit cube by 50.0f, disables face culling, sets depth comparison to D3D11_COMPARISON_LESS_EQUAL, and outputs o.pos = float4(p.x, p.y, p.w, p.w) in SkyboxVS.hlsl so normalized depth equals 1.0 and fills only background pixels untouched by 3D geometry.
  • 2D UI / HUD Pass (RenderSystem::DrawUI): Enables SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA blending, disables depth testing/writing, and sets a top-left pixel orthographic projection (XMMatrixOrthographicOffCenterLH(0, width, height, 0, 0, 1)). Both sprites and font glyphs draw a shared 1x1 unit quad (primitive://quad), passing sub-rectangle UV offsets and scales [uOffset, vOffset, uScale, vScale] through row 0 of b1 (g_View[0]) in SpriteVS.hlsl.

docs.title: Shader Compilation & Bytecode Caching (ShaderManager)
docs.text:
ShaderManager::GetShaderBytecode bridges live authoring and standalone distribution:

  • Editor Mode (!IsVFSActive()): Compiles .hlsl source files at startup via D3DCompileFromFile (vs_5_0 / ps_5_0, adding D3DCOMPILE_DEBUG | D3DCOMPILE_SKIP_OPTIMIZATION in _DEBUG builds), writes the compiled bytecode to shaders/*.cso on disk, and registers the .cso file in AssetManager so PackAssets includes pre-compiled shaders in data.pak.
  • Runtime Mode (IsVFSActive()): Reads pre-compiled shaders/*.cso bytecode directly out of data.pak without requiring .hlsl source files or runtime compilation.

docs.title: Subsystems, Physics, Audio & VFS
docs.text:
Step Engine coordinates its runtime subsystems around two shared hubs: Engine::Scene (which owns the EnTT registry and sol::state Lua VM) and Engine::AssetManager (which maps 64-bit UUIDs to disk paths or data.pak VFS byte ranges).

docs.title: Jolt Physics Integration (PhysicsManager & PhysicsSystem)
docs.text:
PhysicsManager (src/Engine/PhysicsManager.cpp) initializes Jolt Physics with:

  • Memory & Concurrency: A 128 MB JPH::TempAllocatorImpl for lock-free per-step allocations and a JPH::JobSystemThreadPool configured with max(1, hardware_concurrency - 1) worker threads.
  • World Capacity: Up to 10,240 rigid bodies, 65,536 body pairs, and 65,536 contact constraints under standard earth gravity (0.0f, -9.81f, 0.0f).
  • Collision Filtering: Two object and broadphase layers:
    • Layers::NON_MOVING (0) — Static bodies; collides only with MOVING bodies.
    • Layers::MOVING (1) — Dynamic bodies; collides with both NON_MOVING and MOVING bodies.

docs.title: Collider Shapes, Mesh Caching & World Scaling
docs.text:
PhysicsManager::CreatePhysicsShape builds an unscaled base shape from RigidBodyComponent and wraps non-identity world scales (extracted from TransformComponent::worldMatrix via XMMatrixDecompose) in a JPH::ScaledShape:

RBShape Jolt Shape Type Dimensions Used Box JPH::BoxShape halfExtent (x, y, z) scaled by entity world scale Sphere JPH::SphereShape radius scaled by entity world scale Capsule JPH::CapsuleShape halfHeight = height * 0.5f and radius scaled by entity world scale Mesh (Static) JPH::MeshShape Concave indexed triangle list from MeshManager (positions + indices), scaled by worldScale * colliderScale Mesh (Dynamic) JPH::ConvexHullShape Convex hull built from MeshManager::GetMeshPositions, scaled by worldScale * colliderScale

Built mesh shapes are cached in PhysicsManager::m_meshShapeCache keyed by meshID so instancing multiple mesh colliders avoids redundant hull/tree construction. If RigidBodyComponent::meshID is 0 on a Mesh collider, PhysicsSystem automatically wires it from the entity's MeshRendererComponent::meshID.

docs.title: Bidirectional ECS Synchronization
docs.text:
• Play Mode (isPlaying == true):
    1. Steps Jolt with delta time clamped to 1/30 s (0.0333s) across 4 collision sub-steps to prevent high-speed tunneling.
    2. Flushes queued collision callbacks on the main thread.
    3. Pulls world-space position and rotation from JPH::BodyInterface back into TransformComponent. If the entity is parented (RelationshipComponent), PhysicsSystem multiplies by the inverse parent world matrix—querying Jolt directly if the parent also has a RigidBodyComponent to eliminate 1-frame hierarchy lag.
  • Edit Mode (isPlaying == false):
    • Pushes decomposed TransformComponent::worldMatrix changes (from Inspector sliders or ImGuizmo) into Jolt via SetPositionAndRotation and ResetBodyTransform, zeroing linear/angular velocity. If the entity's scale changed, the body is destroyed and invalidated so PhysicsSystem rebuilds its scaled shape and inertia tensor cleanly on the next frame.

docs.title: Hybrid Raycasting & Thread-Safe Contact Events
docs.text:
• Hybrid Raycasting (Scene::CastRay): Queries PhysicsManager::CastRay (1000-unit JPH::RRayCast narrow-phase query) first. If no physics collider is hit, it falls back to testing Engine::Math::RayIntersectsOBB against non-rigidbody active TransformComponent entities (such as lights or uncollided meshes) so Editor viewport picking works on every visible object.
  • Thread-Safe Collision Routing (PhysicsContactListener): Jolt invokes OnContactAdded and OnContactRemoved from worker threads. The listener locks m_eventMutex and records {body1, body2, isEnter} pairs for both directions into m_eventQueue. Immediately after m_physicsSystem->Update(...) finishes, FlushEvents() swaps the queue on the main thread, maps BodyIDs to entt::entity handles in O(N), and invokes OnCollisionEnter(other) / OnCollisionExit(other) on attached Lua scripts.

docs.title: Sandboxed Lua Scripting (sol2)
docs.text:
Gameplay scripts execute inside Scene::m_lua (sol::state with base, math, table, and string standard libraries).

  • Per-Instance Environment Isolation: Each ScriptInstance inside an entity's LuaScriptComponent::scripts vector creates its own sol::environment(scene.m_lua, sol::create, scene.m_lua.globals()) and binds env["self"] = ScriptEntity(entity, &scene). Multiple entities running the same .lua file—or multiple scripts on one entity—never overwrite each other's globals or OnUpdate functions.
  • On-The-Fly Initialization: If a script is attached dynamically during gameplay via Entity:AddLuaScript(filepath), ScriptSystemUpdate detects !script.isInitialized, compiles the script, caches its callbacks, and runs OnCreate() immediately before its first OnUpdate(dt).
  • Memory & Crash Safety:
    • ScriptSystemInit, ScriptSystemUpdate, and ScriptSystemShutdown snapshot entity handles into a local std::vector<entt::entity> and re-fetch component references by index so mid-frame Instantiate calls that reallocate EnTT pools never dangle C++ references.
    • All script loads (safe_script / safe_script_file) and callbacks (sol::protected_function) trap Lua syntax and runtime errors, logging diagnostics to stderr instead of terminating the engine.

docs.title: Spatial Audio (AudioManager & AudioSystem)
docs.text:
AudioManager (src/Engine/AudioManager.cpp) wraps miniaudio (ma_engine) behind opaque void* handles (AudioInstance structs containing ma_sound, ma_decoder, and a std::vector<char> VFS buffer).

  • Editor vs. VFS Decoding: In Editor mode, LoadSound streams/loads from disk via ma_sound_init_from_file. When VFS is active (DIST_BUILD), AudioInstance retains the extracted data.pak byte vector in memory for the lifetime of the sound and decodes it via ma_decoder_init_memory + ma_sound_init_from_data_source.
  • Per-Frame 3D Spatialization (AudioSystem): Updates listener 0 with the active camera's position and quaternion-rotated +Z forward vector, lazily initializes AudioComponent::soundHandle, triggers playOnCreate sounds, stops sounds on deactivated entities, and updates 3D emitter positions from decomposed TransformComponent::worldMatrix translations.

docs.title: UUID Registry & Virtual Asset Paths
docs.text:
AssetManager (src/Engine/AssetManager.cpp) assigns every imported file or procedural resource a random 64-bit Engine::UUID (std::mt19937_64), deduplicating paths so importing the same path twice always returns the existing UUID. In addition to disk filepaths, the engine uses virtual URI conventions:

Virtual Path Pattern AssetType Meaning primitive://cube, primitive://quad, primitive://sphere_..., primitive://capsule_... Mesh Procedural geometry generated by MeshManager primitive://white, primitive://default_normal, primitive://default_orm Texture 1x1 fallback textures generated by TextureManager cubemap://<first_face_path> Texture Combined 6-face cubemap SRV entry (each physical face is also registered individually) shader://basic, shader://unlit, shader://skybox, shader://shadow, shader://sprite Shader Logical shader pipeline identifiers (backed on disk/VFS by shaders/*.cso) <model_path>?mesh=<index> Mesh Individual sub-mesh extracted by Assimp from <model_path> (ModelFile) <ttf_path>?size=<float> Font Baked stb_truetype glyph atlas at a specific pixel height (backed by <ttf_path>)

docs.title: PAK2 Binary Archive Format & Transparent VFS
docs.text:
AssetManager::PackAssets compiles all physical assets in the registry into a single binary data.pak archive:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header (8 bytes)                                                  |
|   char magic[4]      = "PAK2"                                     |
|   uint32_t count     = total registry entries                     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Dynamic Table of Contents (TOC) [repeated `count` times]          |
|   uint64_t uuid      (8 bytes)                                    |
|   uint32_t type      (4 bytes, Engine::AssetType)                 |
|   uint32_t pathLen   (4 bytes)                                    |
|   char filepath[pathLen]                                          |
|   uint64_t offset    (8 bytes, byte offset into payload section)  |
|   uint64_t size      (8 bytes, 0 for virtual/procedural entries)  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Concatenated Raw Binary Payloads                                  |
|   [Raw bytes of models, .mtl/.bin sidecars, textures, .cso,       |
|    audio clips, .ttf fonts, .lua scripts, and .json scenes]       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+

When DX11Runtime calls AssetManager::MountVFS("data.pak"), the engine reconstructs m_assetRegistry and m_vfsTable in memory. Every loader switches seamlessly to memory-buffered reads via ReadAssetFromVFS(uuid)—including Assimp, which uses a custom VFSIOSystem and VFSIOStream (src/Engine/MeshManager.cpp) to resolve .mtl, .bin, and relative model dependencies directly from the archive (and automatically register those sidecar files during Editor imports).

docs.title: Standalone Game Export Pipeline (AssetManager::ExportProject)
docs.text:
Clicking Export Game in the Editor toolbar executes a 5-step packaging pipeline:

flowchart LR
    A["Verify Scene Saved<br/>(GetCurrentScenePath != empty)"] --> B["Clean & Create<br/>ExportedGame/"]
    B --> C["SceneSerializer::Serialize<br/>(Register all attached scripts)"]
    C --> D["AssetManager::PackAssets<br/>-> ExportedGame/data.pak"]
    D --> E["Copy RuntimeTemplate/<br/>(DX11Runtime.exe + *.dll)"]
    E --> F["Write ExportedGame/enginefiles/Launch.txt<br/>& Open in Explorer"]

docs.title: Adding & Managing Assets
docs.text: Step Engine organizes project content inside the assets/ directory and tracks every imported resource using a persistent 64-bit Engine::UUID stored in enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json.

docs.title: Asset Directory Conventions & Supported Formats
docs.text:
During CMake builds, the CopyAssets target copies the root assets/ folder into ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin/assets/ (the working directory of DX11Editor in Visual Studio).

Important Working Directory Tip: When running DX11Editor from Visual Studio, the working directory is ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin (e.g., out/build/x64-Debug/bin). Place new assets inside the repository's assets/ folder so they remain tracked in Git and get copied on build—or copy them into both assets/ and bin/assets/ if adding files while the editor is already open.

Subdirectory Supported Extensions Drag-and-Drop Payload Used By assets/Models/ .obj (+ .mtl), .fbx, .gltf (+ .bin), .glb MODEL_FILE MeshManager, Scene::InstantiateModel, MeshRendererComponent, RigidBodyComponent (Mesh) assets/Textures/ .png, .jpg, .jpeg TEXTURE_FILE TextureManager, MeshRendererComponent (Albedo / Normal / ORM), SpriteRendererComponent assets/Audio/ .wav, .mp3 AUDIO_FILE AudioManager, AudioComponent assets/Fonts/ .ttf FONT_FILE FontManager, TextRendererComponent assets/Scripts/ .lua SCRIPT_FILE LuaScriptComponent, ScriptSystem assets/Scenes/ .json (Click to load) SceneSerializer, EditorUI Content Browser

(Windows paths are case-insensitive, so assets/Audio and assets/audio resolve identically on Windows, though keeping consistent relative paths with forward slashes / is recommended for VFS compatibility.)

docs.title: Via the Editor (Drag-and-Drop)
docs.text:
1. Place your model file (and any companion .mtl or .bin files) under assets/Models/<YourModel>/.
  2. Open the Content Browser panel at the bottom of DX11Editor and navigate to the model file.
  3. Drag the .obj, .fbx, .gltf, or .glb entry from the Content Browser into the empty space at the bottom of the Hierarchy panel.
  4. Scene::InstantiateModel automatically:
    • Parses the file with Assimp (Triangulate, FlipUVs, MakeLeftHanded, FlipWindingOrder, PreTransformVertices, CalcTangentSpace).
    • Registers the container file (AssetType::ModelFile), any .mtl/.bin sidecars opened through VFSIOSystem, and each sub-mesh (<filepath>?mesh=<i>).
    • Creates a root parent entity named after the file stem (e.g., ABeautifulGame) and attaches child entities (ABeautifulGame_mesh_0, ABeautifulGame_mesh_1, ...) each equipped with a MeshRendererComponent.

docs.title: Adding a Mesh Collider
docs.text:
To give an imported sub-mesh physical collision:

  1. Select the child sub-mesh entity in the Hierarchy.
  2. In the Inspector, click Add Component -> Rigidbody.
  3. Change Shape to Mesh:
    • Choose Motion Type Static for level geometry or props that do not move (builds an exact concave JPH::MeshShape).
    • Choose Motion Type Dynamic for movable physics objects (automatically builds a JPH::ConvexHullShape).
  4. PhysicsSystem automatically wires RigidBodyComponent::meshID from the entity's MeshRendererComponent::meshID. Adjust Collider Scale if needed and verify alignment using the Show Wireframe green overlay.

docs.title: Via Lua at Runtime
docs.text:
Attach a custom MeshRendererComponent and assign a specific sub-mesh index (?mesh=0, ?mesh=1, etc.):

self:AddMeshRenderer(MeshType.Custom)
self:SetMesh("assets/Models/container/model/container.obj?mesh=0")

docs.title: 2. Assigning PBR Materials & Textures
docs.text: MeshRendererComponent uses a metallic-roughness PBR workflow when Material Type is set to Textured.

docs.title: Texture Channel Packing Rules
docs.text:
Slot Shader Register Expected Format & Channels Default Fallback (if cleared / 0) Albedo (Color) t0 RGBA base color map (multiplied by Base Color tint) 1x1 Pure White (255, 255, 255, 255) Normal Map t1 Tangent-space DirectX normal map (+Y down / DirectX convention) 1x1 Flat Z-Up (128, 128, 255, 255) ORM Map t2 R = Ambient Occlusion, G = Roughness, B = Metallic 1x1 (255, 128, 0, 255) (AO=1, Rough=0.5, Metal=0)

Roughness & Metallic Multipliers: In BasicPS.hlsl, sampled ORM channels are multiplied by the component's scalar sliders (roughness = orm.g * g_Roughness, metallic = orm.b * g_Metallic). When using an ORM map that encodes metallic detail in the Blue channel, set the Inspector Metallic slider above 0.0 (e.g., 1.0) so metallic regions are not multiplied to zero!

docs.title: Steps in the Inspector
docs.text:
1. Select an entity with a Mesh Renderer component.
  2. Change Material Type to Textured.
  3. Drag .png or .jpg files from the Content Browser onto the Albedo (Color), Normal Map, and ORM drop zones (or click X next to any slot to revert to its 1x1 fallback texture).
  4. Tune the Roughness and Metallic sliders to scale the surface response.

docs.title: 2D Sprites
docs.text:
1. Select an entity (or create an Empty Entity in the Hierarchy for HUD elements).
  2. Click Add Component -> Sprite Renderer.
  3. Drag a .png / .jpg image from the Content Browser onto the Sprite Texture drop zone.
  4. Set screen-space Position (X,Y) and Size (W,H) in pixels ((0, 0) is the top-left of the viewport), Pivot (0-1) ((0.5, 0.5) centers the sprite), Rotation (degrees), and Tint Color.

docs.title: Dynamic Text & .ttf Fonts
docs.text:
1. Place .ttf font files inside assets/Fonts/ (e.g., assets/Fonts/FiraCode-VariableFont_wght.ttf).
  2. Select an entity and click Add Component -> Text Renderer.
  3. Select your .ttf file from the Font dropdown in the Inspector.
  4. Adjust Font Size (8–256 px), Text, Position (X,Y), and Color.
    • Changing the font file or size automatically bakes a 2048x2048 RGBA glyph atlas (stb_truetype, ASCII 32–126) under the virtual asset path <filepath>?size=<fontSize>.

docs.title: 4. Adding Audio Clips
docs.text:
1. Place .wav or .mp3 files inside assets/Audio/.
  2. Select an entity in the Hierarchy and click Add Component -> Audio Component.
  3. Choose the audio clip from the Audio File dropdown, or drag the .wav/.mp3 file from the Content Browser onto the combo box.
  4. Configure playback behavior:
    • Is 3D: Enables 3D distance attenuation and panning relative to the active camera listener. Disable (false) for 2D background music or UI sound effects.
    • Looping: Repeats continuously while playing.
    • Play On Create: Automatically starts playback as soon as Play Mode begins.
    • Volume: Clamped between 0.0 (mute) and 1.0 (full gain).

docs.title: 5. Customizing the Skybox
docs.text:
By default, LoadCoreAssets() in src/main.cpp loads six cubemap faces in DirectX +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z order:

  1. assets/Textures/Skybox/right.png (+X)
  2. assets/Textures/Skybox/left.png (-X)
  3. assets/Textures/Skybox/top.png (+Y)
  4. assets/Textures/Skybox/bottom.png (-Y)
  5. assets/Textures/Skybox/front.png (+Z)
  6. assets/Textures/Skybox/back.png (-Z)

All six images must share identical pixel dimensions. You can replace those six .png files directly or pass a custom 6-element vector to TextureManager::LoadCubemap and Renderer::SetSkybox.

docs.title: How AssetRegistry.json & VFS Packing Work
docs.text:
• Whenever AssetManager::ImportAsset encounters a new file path, it generates a random 64-bit UUID.
  • Saving a scene (Ctrl + S) or closing DX11Editor writes all known (UUID, Filepath, Type) entries to enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json.
  • Do not delete enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json once you have saved .json scenes under assets/Scenes/—scene files reference meshes, textures, fonts, and audio clips by their 64-bit UUIDs! If an asset referenced by a scene is missing from the registry or deleted from disk, SceneSerializer::Deserialize safely aborts loading and displays a Scene Validation Failed modal explaining which asset type is missing.

docs.title: Creating, Editing & Exporting Scenes
docs.text: DX11Editor provides a dockable authoring workspace for assembling 3D worlds, tuning lighting and physics, playtesting in-editor, and exporting standalone executables.

docs.title: Editor Workspace & Controls
docs.text:
When DX11Editor launches, EditorUI::SetupDockspace arranges five dockable panels:

  • Toolbar (Top) — Play / Stop state toggle and Export Game button.
  • Hierarchy (Left) — Scene entity tree, context-menu spawning, and drag-and-drop parenting.
  • Scene Viewport (Center) — Off-screen DirectX 11 render view, object picking, and ImGuizmo handles.
  • Inspector (Right) — Active toggles, component properties, and Add / Remove Component menus.
  • Content Browser (Bottom) — File explorer rooted at assets/, scene loader, and drag-and-drop asset source.

docs.title: Viewport Navigation & Shortcuts
docs.text: Input Action Right Mouse Button (Hold) (in Scene panel) Captures cursor for free-look camera rotation W / A / S / D (while RMB held) Fly forward, left, backward, and right Left Shift (while flying, or while Scene focused) Multiplies fly speed by sprintMultiplier (2.0x default) Mouse Wheel (while Scene focused) Dolly camera forward / backward along view vector Left Mouse Button (in Scene panel) Raycast pick entity (Jolt narrow-phase first, OBB fallback) Space (while Scene focused in Edit mode) Cycle ImGuizmo mode: Translate -> Rotate -> Scale Delete (while Hierarchy focused) Destroy selected entity (cascades to all children) Ctrl + S Save current scene (opens Save Scene As modal if unsaved) Escape Close application

docs.title: Step 1: Create a New Scene
docs.text:
1. Right-click empty space inside the Content Browser panel and select Create New Scene.
  2. Enter a scene name (e.g., Level01) and click Create.
  3. The editor invokes Scene::GenerateDefaultSetup, saves assets/Scenes/Level01.json, and updates the Scene tab title. Every new scene starts with four pre-configured entities:
    • Editor Camera (hidden from Hierarchy) — Fly camera used while authoring in Edit mode.
    • Main Camera — In-game camera automatically activated when entering Play mode or running a standalone export.
    • Sun Light — White Directional light (intensity = 5.0) pitched down at 45° to drive Cascaded Shadow Maps.
    • Ground — Static 20 x 0.1 x 20 box mesh and RigidBodyComponent at (0, -5, 0).

docs.title: Spawning Built-In Entities
docs.text:
Right-click empty space in the Hierarchy panel and choose Create New Entity:

  • Empty Entity — IDComponent + NameComponent + TransformComponent (ideal for hierarchy folders, script managers, audio emitters, or 2D HUD elements).
  • Camera — Creates a new game CameraComponent + ViewportComponent.
  • Shapes -> Cube, Sphere, or Capsule — Spawns a primitive MeshRendererComponent.
  • Lights -> Directional Light, Point Light, or Spot Light — Spawns a LightComponent (up to 16 active frustum-visible lights render simultaneously; the first active Directional light casts 3-cascade shadows).

docs.title: Building Parent-Child Hierarchies
docs.text:
• Parent an Entity: Drag an entity node in the Hierarchy and drop it onto another entity node. Its world position, rotation, and scale remain unchanged while its TransformComponent converts into parent-relative local space.
  • Unparent to Root: Drag a child entity node and drop it onto the empty space below the list in the Hierarchy panel.
  • Remove a Component: Right-click any framed component header (Light, Rigidbody, Mesh Renderer, Audio Emitter, Lua Scripts, Sprite Renderer, Text Renderer) in the Inspector and click Remove Component.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
• Press Ctrl + S.
  • If the scene has not been saved yet (such as the startup sandbox), the Save Scene As modal opens and writes assets/Scenes/<Name>.json.
  • Subsequent Ctrl + S presses overwrite the active .json file and update enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json so any newly attached Lua scripts or imported assets are recorded.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
1. Ensure the Editor is in Edit mode (scenes cannot be loaded while Play mode is running).
  2. In the Content Browser, navigate into Scenes (assets/Scenes/) and click [SCENE] <Name>.json.
  3. SceneSerializer::Deserialize validates every asset UUID and script path before clearing the current scene, reconstructs all entities and hierarchies, and preloads referenced models and textures into VRAM.

docs.title: Scene JSON Structure Example
docs.text:
Scenes are stored in human-readable JSON so diffs remain clean in version control:

{
    "Scene": [
        {
            "EntityID": 2,
            "NameComponent": {
                "Name": "Main Camera",
                "IsActive": true
            },
            "TransformComponent": {
                "Position": [0.0, 0.0, -10.0],
                "Rotation": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
                "Scale": [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
            },
            "CameraComponent": {
                "FOV": 0.7853981852531433,
                "NearClip": 0.10000000149011612,
                "FarClip": 500.0,
                "InvertY": true
            }
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Step 4: Playtest & Export a Standalone Game
Non-Destructive Playtesting
docs.text:
1. Verify your scene has at least one active Camera entity (such as Main Camera).
  2. Click Play in the top Toolbar:
    • The Editor snapshots the world (CopyToBackup()), hides authoring panels, switches to your game camera, runs OnCreate() on all Lua scripts, and begins stepping Jolt Physics and 3D audio.
  3. Click Stop to invoke OnDestroy(), tear down runtime physics/audio handles, and restore the exact pre-play scene state.

docs.title: Exporting a Standalone Build (ExportedGame/)
docs.text:
1. Prerequisite: Build the DX11Runtime target (or Build -> Build All in Visual Studio) at least once so ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin/RuntimeTemplate/ contains DX11Runtime.exe and its required .dll dependencies.
  2. Save your startup scene (Ctrl + S) while in Edit mode.
  3. Click Export Game in the Toolbar.
  4. AssetManager::ExportProject automatically assembles ${WorkingDir}/ExportedGame/: 
    ExportedGame/
├── DX11Runtime.exe          # Standalone game executable (DIST_BUILD)
├── *.dll                    # Required runtime DLLs (SDL2, assimp, lua, etc.)
├── data.pak                 # Packed PAK2 VFS archive (all assets, .cso shaders, scripts, scenes)
└── enginefiles/
    └── Launch.txt           # Relative path to the exported startup scene JSON
  5. Windows Explorer opens ExportedGame/ automatically—double-click DX11Runtime.exe to run the standalone game!

docs.title: Writing Lua Gameplay Scripts
docs.text:
Step Engine embeds Lua via sol2 so you can write gameplay logic, physics interactions, entity spawners, and dynamic HUD updates without recompiling C++.

For the complete signature list of every bound type and enum, see Lua Scripting Bindings.

docs.title: Step 1: Create & Attach a Script
docs.text:
1. Create a new .lua file inside assets/Scripts/ (for example, assets/Scripts/PlayerController.lua). (If DX11Editor is running from bin/, ensure the file is also copied into bin/assets/Scripts/ or run a quick CMake build so CopyAssets syncs it.)
  2. Select the target entity in the Hierarchy panel.
  3. In the Inspector, click Add Component -> Lua Script.
  4. Click Add Script Slot, then either:
    • Choose PlayerController.lua from the dropdown list, or
    • Drag PlayerController.lua directly from the Content Browser onto the script slot (or onto the Add Script Slot button to append a new slot in one step).

You can attach multiple scripts to the same entity. Each slot executes inside its own sandboxed sol::environment with self bound to the owning Entity.

docs.title: Step 2: Implement Lifecycle & Collision Callbacks
docs.text:
Every script can define up to five engine callbacks:

-- Local variables stay private to this specific ScriptInstance!
local elapsed = 0.0

function OnCreate()
    print(self:GetName() .. " spawned!")
end

function OnUpdate(dt)
    elapsed = elapsed + dt
end

function OnCollisionEnter(other)
    print(self:GetName() .. " hit " .. other:GetName())
end

function OnCollisionExit(other)
    print(self:GetName() .. " separated from " .. other:GetName())
end

function OnDestroy()
    print(self:GetName() .. " cleaned up after " .. tostring(elapsed) .. "s")
end

docs.title: Recipe 1: Physics-Driven Player Movement & Jumping
docs.text:
Ensure the entity has a Dynamic Rigidbody component attached in the Inspector (or via AddRigidBody in OnCreate), then apply impulses or velocities based on Input:

local moveForce = 0.25
local jumpImpulse = 6.0

function OnUpdate(dt)
    local dx = 0.0
    local dz = 0.0

    if Input:IsKeyDown(Key.W) then dz = dz + 1.0 end
    if Input:IsKeyDown(Key.S) then dz = dz - 1.0 end
    if Input:IsKeyDown(Key.A) then dx = dx - 1.0 end
    if Input:IsKeyDown(Key.D) then dx = dx + 1.0 end

    if dx ~= 0.0 or dz ~= 0.0 then
        self:ApplyLinearImpulse(dx * moveForce, 0.0, dz * moveForce)
    end

    if Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.Space) then
        self:ApplyLinearImpulse(0.0, jumpImpulse, 0.0)
    end
end

docs.title: Recipe 2: Runtime Spawning, Audio & Timed Destruction
docs.text:
You can spawn new entities, attach meshes/colliders/audio/scripts dynamically, and schedule automatic cleanup using Destroy(delay):

-- Spawner.lua
function OnUpdate(dt)
    if Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.Space) then
        local ball = self:Instantiate("Bouncing Ball")
        local pos = self:GetTransform().position
        ball:GetTransform():SetPosition(pos.x, pos.y + 2.0, pos.z)

        ball:AddMeshRenderer(MeshType.Sphere)
        -- RBShape.Sphere, Dynamic motion, radius=0.5, mass=1.0, restitution=0.8
        ball:AddRigidBody(RBShape.Sphere, RBMotion.Dynamic, 0.5, 1.0, 0.8)
        ball:AddAudioComponent("assets/Audio/spawn.mp3", true, false, true)

        -- Automatically destroy the spawned ball after 5 seconds
        ball:Destroy(5.0)
    end
end

docs.title: Recipe 3: Forward Raycasting
docs.text:
Use self:GetForwardVector() and Physics.CastRay to detect objects in front of an entity. Offset the ray origin slightly outside the caster's own collider to avoid self-hits:

function OnUpdate(dt)
    if Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.F) then
        local pos = self:GetTransform().position
        local fwd = self:GetForwardVector()

        local ox = pos.x + fwd.x * 0.6
        local oy = pos.y + fwd.y * 0.6
        local oz = pos.z + fwd.z * 0.6

        local hit = Physics.CastRay(ox, oy, oz, fwd.x, fwd.y, fwd.z)
        if hit ~= nil then
            print("Hit entity: " .. hit:GetName())
        end
    end
end

docs.title: Recipe 4: Scene Queries & Hierarchy Reparenting
docs.text:
Locate another entity by name with Scene.FindEntityByName and attach it as a child while preserving its world transform:

function OnCreate()
    local weapon = Scene.FindEntityByName("LaserRifle")
    if weapon ~= nil then
        weapon:SetParent(self)
    end
end

docs.title: Recipe 5: Dynamic 2D HUD & Game Restart / Quit
docs.text:
Configure screen-space text and sprites or trigger level restarts directly from Lua:

local score = 0

function OnCreate()
    self:AddTextRenderer()
    self:SetFont("assets/Fonts/FiraCode-VariableFont_wght.ttf", 32)
    self:SetTextPosition(24.0, 24.0)
    self:SetTextColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    self:SetText("Score: 0")
end

function OnUpdate(dt)
    if Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.E) then
        score = score + 10
        self:SetText("Score: " .. tostring(score))
    end

    if Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.R) then
        Game.Restart()
    elseif Input:IsKeyPressed(Key.Q) then
        Game.Quit()
    end
end

docs.title: Pitfalls & Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Colon (:) vs. Dot (.) Call Syntax:
    • Use colon syntax on usertype instances (self:..., other:..., tc:SetPosition(...), and Input:IsKeyDown(...)).
    • Use dot syntax on global namespace tables (Physics.CastRay(...), Scene.FindEntityByName(...), Time.deltaTime, Game.Restart(), Game.Quit()).
  2. Updating TransformComponent Position & Scale:
    • self:GetTransform().position returns a Vector3 by value. Do not write self:GetTransform().position.x = 10—that modifies a temporary copy without setting isDirty = true.
    • Instead, call self:GetTransform():SetPosition(x, y, z) or assign a Vector3 (self:GetTransform().position = Vector3.new(x, y, z)).
  3. Moving Dynamic Rigid Bodies:
    • During Play Mode, PhysicsSystem overwrites TransformComponent positions of active RigidBodyComponent entities from Jolt every frame. Move physics-enabled entities using ApplyLinearImpulse or SetLinearVelocity rather than SetPosition.
  4. Standalone VFS Compatibility:
    • Any script attached via AddLuaScript("assets/Scripts/Foo.lua") or asset loaded dynamically via AddAudioComponent / SetAlbedo / SetFont in a standalone DX11Runtime build must already be registered in enginefiles/AssetRegistry.json prior to clicking Export Game so that PackAssets includes it inside data.pak. Playtesting your scene once in DX11Editor and pressing Ctrl + S before exporting guarantees that dynamic assets are registered!
